Share on X Telegram Enugu Rangers will seek to protect their two-goal advantage when they face MC Alger in a potentially tense CAF Champions League second preliminary round return leg in Algiers on Friday.
The Nigerian champions take a 2-0 lead into the encounter at the Stade Ali Ammar in Douéra, with kick-off scheduled for 8pm local time, but controversy surrounding the first leg has heightened concerns ahead of the decisive fixture.
Beyond the battle for a place in the group stage, the match comes amid a dispute over alleged crowd violence, vandalism and officiating during the first leg at the MKO Abiola Stadium in Abeokuta.
Rangers have petitioned the Confederation of African Football (CAF), alleging that sections of the visiting supporters caused damage to stadium facilities and engaged in acts of violence.
The Enugu club claimed that more than 400 MC Alger supporters were involved in the unrest, alleging that they destroyed an entrance gate, gained unauthorised entry into the stadium and vandalised seats in the covered stands.
Rangers also alleged that their assistant coach was attacked and said they had submitted photographs and video recordings to CAF in support of their complaint.
The club called for urgent intervention by the continental governing body, including precautionary measures ahead of the return leg and reimbursement for revenue allegedly lost during the incident.
MC Alger, however, have rejected the vandalism allegations, insisting that evidence in their possession shows some of the affected seats were damaged before the match.
The Algerian club has also challenged the officiating in the first leg, questioning the penalty awarded to Rangers and the second yellow card shown to midfielder Oussama Benhaoua, whom it claimed was punished for an offence committed by teammate Ayoub Ghezala.
MC Alger further alleged that members of their delegation were harassed in the VIP section and that their cameraman was interfered with during a live broadcast. The club also complained about the cost of tickets for travelling supporters.
The competing accounts have added an off-field dimension to a tie that will determine which side advances to the next stage of Africa’s premier club competition.
CAF has responded to the security concerns by appointing Ugandan security expert Dixon Okello as security officer for Friday’s encounter.
The governing body also named Egypt’s Hisham Salaheldin Mostafa as match commissioner, Lesotho’s David Molise as referee and Togo’s Koku Ognankotan Ntale as referee assessor.
The appointments underline the importance of security and match management ahead of the fixture, although they do not resolve the underlying dispute between the clubs.
Rangers are still awaiting a substantive decision on their petition, while no sanction against MC Alger has been announced in the information provided ahead of the return leg.
On the pitch, Rangers face an opponent determined to overturn the deficit in front of its home supporters.
MC Alger held a meeting on Wednesday involving captain Ayoub Abdelouali and head coach Khaled Ben Yahia, with the players reportedly pledging to produce a comeback and win by at least three goals.
The Algerian side will be without suspended defender Oussama Benhaoua and injured captain Ayoub Abdellaoui, but midfielder Mohamed Benkhemassa and forward Ben Ahmed Kohili are available again.
MC Alger can also draw inspiration from their history against Rangers.
In 1976, the Algerian club overturned a 2-0 first-leg deficit against the Nigerian side in the semi-finals of the African Cup of Champions Clubs, winning 3-0 in Algiers before going on to claim the title.
Although that comeback occurred almost five decades ago, it offers the hosts a reminder that Rangers’ advantage is far from insurmountable.
For Rangers, the challenge will be to remain disciplined and composed under pressure while resisting the temptation to defend too deep for the entire match.
Nigeria Premier Football League chief operating officer Ayo Abdulrahman has warned the players to expect a difficult atmosphere, urging them to remain focused and respond appropriately to developments on the pitch.
“It’s not going to be a tea party, don’t expect them to offer you flowers,” Abdulrahman warned.
He urged the Flying Antelopes to “stay focused, take the fight to them, and respond to the dictates of the game, especially when you have to defend”.
Technical adviser Fidelis Ilechukwu has also cautioned his players against relaxing despite their first-leg advantage.
Rangers must balance defensive organisation with the need to threaten on the counter-attack, knowing that an away goal would increase the pressure on the hosts.
Their ability to manage the opening stages could prove decisive, particularly if MC Alger score early and ignite the home crowd’s hopes of a comeback.
The Nigerian side arrived safely in Algeria, but the security arrangements surrounding the match will remain under scrutiny following the allegations arising from the first leg.
Rangers have the advantage of a two-goal lead, but MC Alger possess both home support and a historical precedent for overturning the same deficit against the Nigerian club.
